practice1.prompt: rebuild the call chain so the traceback names both functions

hiddenCases.name: a single number averages to itself
an empty list still raises ZeroDivisionError
process_data hands its work to calculate_average
hiddenCases.describe: two functions, with process_data calling calculate_average

hiddenCases.name: the error is let out, not caught
hiddenCases.describe: no try/except, so the traceback can show both frames

practice1.hint: Two frames is the whole point of the exercise: the empty list is passed in one function and divided by in another, so both names appear in the traceback. Catching the error would collapse that chain into nothing.

questions.prompt: Where in a traceback is the error that actually stopped the program?
questions.explain: Python prints the frames oldest first and the error last. Reading from the bottom gives you what broke before you work back through who asked for it.

questions.prompt: What do the lines above the error message tell you?
choices: The chain of calls that led to the line that broke
questions.explain: Each frame is one call still in progress. The chain is how a bad value that entered at the top ends up dividing by zero somewhere near the bottom.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of reading a traceback in the order the lesson recommends.
items: Work back up the frames to find where the bad value came from
Read the last line for the error type and message
Look at the line just above it to see which line of your code raised it
questions.explain: What broke, then where, then why. Starting at the top of a long traceback usually means reading through library code that has nothing wrong with it.

questions.prompt: Why does catching the exception make this bug harder to diagnose?
choices: The traceback is never printed, so the call chain that explains the failure is lost
It does not, catching is always better
questions.explain: The traceback is only produced when nothing handles the exception. Catching it early, before you understand it, discards the one report that named both functions.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Say where you start reading and what the lines above that tell you. Bottom first is the habit worth stating.

reflection-exercise2.hint: Three errors by name, what each one is telling you, and what you would change. The name is the part that narrows the search.
